# WIPI Java surface entries this runtime deliberately does not register.
# Every other line of testdata/wipi_java_surface.txt must be implemented;
# TestRuntimeJavaSurfaceCoversReference fails on a gap that is not listed
# here and on a line here that has since been implemented.

# Bridge constructors that exist only because the original implementation
# builds WIPI on top of its own MIDP classes. This runtime owns the WIPI
# classes directly, so there is no javax.microedition object to wrap and no
# guest can name these types.
org/kwis/msp/db/DataBase <init> (Ljavax/microedition/rms/RecordStore;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Card setCanvas (Ljavax/microedition/lcdui/Canvas;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Display <init> (Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/Jlet;Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/DisplayProxy;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Font <init> (Ljavax/microedition/lcdui/Font;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Graphics <init> (Ljavax/microedition/lcdui/Graphics;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Graphics <init> (Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/Display;)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Image <init> ()V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Image <init> (Ljavax/microedition/lcdui/Image;)V

# Font has no class initializer here: the runtime font is a single shared
# object created on first request rather than a table of static instances.
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Font <clinit> ()V

# Card.paint is abstract. Guest subclasses declare it in their own AOT
# metadata and the paint service dispatches to that by name, so declaring it
# on the runtime class would add a vtable slot no guest class inherits.
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Card paint (Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/Graphics;)V

# Raw device-format pixel transfers and image encoding. The byte layout and
# the encoded format are device-specific and unconfirmed; the 0x00RRGGBB
# transfers (getRGBPixels/setRGBPixels) are implemented instead.
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Graphics getPixels (IIII[BII)V
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Graphics setPixels (IIII[BII)V

# Animated images. No animated format is decoded, so there is no frame clock
# to drive, and the ImageObserver completion protocol (its status argument) is
# unconfirmed — the original emulator stubs these for the same reason, so
# there is nothing to compare an implementation against. Failing loudly beats
# inventing a callback contract a game would then branch on.
#
# play and stop have left this list. They are not the callback contract: the
# specification says both do nothing for an image that is not animated, which
# every image here is, so answering that is the contract rather than a guess.
# See the stub inventory.
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Image loadImage (Ljava/lang/String;Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/ImageObserver;)Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/Image;
org/kwis/msp/lcdui/Image stopImage (Lorg/kwis/msp/lcdui/ImageObserver;)V
